newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish bourse suffers drought ahead FOMC, Easter.
newsitem.headline: Finnish bourse suffers drought ahead FOMC, Easter.

text.p: Shares fell on Monday and the session was the year's least active with volume barely half the normal level due to uncertainty ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting FOMC meeting, brokers said.
Trading was also dented by approaching Easter holiday.
The HEX general index fell 0.67 percent to close at 2,819.22 points and the FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark ended down 0.74 percent at 984.14. Volume was just 310 million markka.
"This has been the quietest day so far this year," one broker said. "I don't see any action tomorrow either."
Investors discounted a 25 basis point rise in the U.S. key rate from 5.25 percent, brokers said.
"If the Fed raises rates more, stocks will fall, but if they leave rates unchanged stocks will fall," one broker said, adding that unchanged rates would increase uncertainty.
Other brokers said bond and stock markets would take a favourable view and rally if the Fed did not lift rates.
Generous dividends for 1996 attracted investors to pharmaceuticals group Orion whose B share rose 3.00 markka to 180.00 and was the most traded stock, brokers said.
Engineering group Metra's B share rose 5.00 markka to 295.00 on its dividend and one-for-one bonus issue, they said.

Telecoms group and bourse engine Nokia fell 2.50 markka to 303.00 and was relegated to an unsusual third place on the list of most traded stocks, accounting for less than 20 percent of trade due to the generally sluggish market.
